summary: String methods clean up, search, slice, and split text. Each one returns a new string, so you save the result in a variable.
notes: course.slice(1, 4) includes index 1 and stops before index 4. slice(4) goes to the end.
indexOf() returns -1 when the text is not found. includes() returns true or false.
split(",") returns an array. names.join(" | ") is called on the array, with the separator as the argument.
pitfall: replace() changes only the first match: "9-10-11".replace("-", "/") gives "9/10-11". Use replaceAll() to change every match.
contrast: Strings are immutable in all three. JavaScript's s.slice(1, 4) works like Java's substring(1, 4), and join() is called on the array (names.join(" | ")), the reverse of Python's " | ".join(names).
